title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: When medical cost trend accelerates faster than your annual bid assumptions, there is no shortcut—you must reprice the book, exit unprofitable footprints, and rebuild reserve credibility quarter by quarter.
epigraph.author: Executive Accountability & KPI Audit, 2022–2026

web_blocks.title: Six Core Operational KPIs Governing Enterprise Health

web_blocks.html: Judging UnitedHealth Group solely on reported EPS misses the early operating signals that flag margin turns 12 to 18 months ahead. Six operational KPIs drive the business across UnitedHealthcare and Optum. These are: (1) consolidated Medical Care Ratio (MCR), (2) CMS Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, (3) Days Claims Payable (DCP), (4) Optum Health value-based care (VBC) patients, (5) Optum Rx adjusted scripts, and (6) Optum Insight contract backlog [1], [3], [4], [15].

web_blocks.takeaway: Core insurance underwriting (MCR 88.4%, DCP 47.0 days) and Optum Rx/Insight execution have stabilized in 2026, but the 2027 Star Ratings drop to 68%–71% and Optum Health VBC restructuring keep KPI health on watch.

web_blocks.html: Looking past 2026, UnitedHealth Group's structural growth engine remains anchored by steady demographic tailwinds. Over 10,000 Americans age into Medicare each day, specialty biologics and GLP-1 drugs lift Optum Rx volume, and hospital labor inflation pushes health systems toward Optum Insight's AI revenue-cycle outsourcing [4], [18]. Management has reiterated its goal to return to its long-term 13%–16% annual earnings growth algorithm entering 2027 [4]. However, investors must temper that optimism against two concrete headwinds. First, CMS's CY 2027 Final Rate Notice gives only a +2.48% net average payment update, down from +5.06% in CY 2026 [9], [10]. Second, the October 2026 release of 2027 Star Ratings showed 4+ star enrollment sliding from ~81% to ~68%–71%. Average contract ratings also fell from 3.82 to 3.57 [15]. Because Star Ratings govern 5% quality bonuses in payment year 2028, UHC must offset that drag with tighter benefit design and AI automation.

A rigorous Walk-the-Talk audit across 2022–2026 reveals a stark split between the Witty/Rex era's overpromising and the Hemsley/DeVeydt era's blunt reset. In 2022–2023, then-CEO Andrew Witty and CFO John Rex repeatedly assured investors that Medicare Advantage bids fully priced post-pandemic care catch-up. They also claimed Optum Health's rapid expansion to 4.7 million value-based care patients would compound margins smoothly [16], [22]. In reality, two major execution failures built up beneath the surface. First was cybersecurity governance: Change Healthcare ran legacy perimeter systems without universal multi-factor login, culminating in the February 2024 ransomware breach that cost $2.3B–$2.45B [14]. Second was underwriting & V28 mispricing: management underestimated CMS V28 risk-score cuts and senior outpatient demand. That miss forced guidance suspensions in early 2025 as FY2025 operating earnings fell 41% to $18.96 billion [3], [16].

The board's May 2025 decision to bring back Stephen Hemsley as CEO marked a decisive accountability pivot. It was followed in September 2025 by hiring veteran managed-care CFO Wayne DeVeydt alongside segment chiefs Tim Noel (UHC) and Dr. Patrick Conway (Optum) [7], [8]. Rather than defending empty top-line volume, Hemsley and DeVeydt explicitly cut 1.8 million lower-margin lives in 2026 and exited South America. They also pruned underwater Optum Health capitation contracts and rebuilt Days Claims Payable back to 47.0–48.6 days [4], [5], [22]. That conservatism restored guidance credibility across the market. After setting cautious initial 2026 targets, management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance in October 2026 to at least $20.50 (GAAP EPS at least $19.50). That raise was backed by $610 million of favorable prior-period reserve development in Q3 2026 [4].

web_blocks.title: Walk-the-Talk Watchlist: DOJ Probes & 2027 Star Ratings
paragraphs: Hemsley and DeVeydt earned quick credibility by under-promising and over-delivering on 2026 MCR recovery. Still, legacy governance overhangs persist, including DOJ civil and criminal probes into Medicare Advantage risk coding and Optum Rx, plus shareholder suits over prior-management statements [17].
At the same time, the drop in 2027 Star Ratings to 68%–71% in 4+ star plans shows that member experience and clinical quality still lag peak standards [15].

web_blocks.html: Tracking the sequential cadence across 2026 confirms that operational repair is broad-based rather than a one-quarter fluke. After posting 44.1 Days Claims Payable in Q4 2025, management rebuilt DCP to 48.6 days in Q1 2026. It then maintained 47.0 days across both Q2 and Q3 2026 [3], [4], [5], [6]. Nine-month 2026 consolidated revenues totaled $336,447 million, while operating earnings reached $23,544 million (a 7.00% margin). Net earnings attributable to common shareholders reached $15,874 million over the same nine-month span [19]. In Q3 2026 specifically, UnitedHealthcare generated $2.8 billion of operating earnings (3.3% margin) while Optum generated $3.7 billion (5.5% margin). That performance enabled management to lift full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 [4].

On the October 13, 2026 Q3 earnings call, CEO Stephen Hemsley framed the turnaround directly: "Our third quarter performance reflects actions taken throughout 2026, driving meaningful progress and reinforcing our confidence to sustainably grow in 2027 and beyond within our 13% to 16% long-term target growth range." [19] CFO Wayne DeVeydt added: "We're steadily and methodically improving performance broadly across the portfolio. We are positioned to finish 2026 strongly, and we remain focused on consistently delivering our 13 to 16 percent long-term growth target." [19] Whether management clears that 13%–16% bar depends on 2027 Optum Health margin recovery and 2028 Star Rating remediation.

book_paragraphs: If you want to know whether UnitedHealth Group's turnaround is genuine or merely accounting smoke, you and I have to ignore headline adjusted EPS for a moment and inspect six leading operational dials on the dashboard. In managed care, those six dials tell you where margins will be twelve months before the income statement catches up.

Dial number one is the Medical Care Ratio. After hovering in the low-to-mid 80s for years, UNH's MCR surged to 89.1% in FY2025 and hit 89.9% in the third quarter of 2025. By Q3 2026, under Stephen Hemsley's repricing discipline, the MCR dropped 150 basis points year-over-year to 88.4%, helped by $610 million of favorable prior-period reserve development on 2026 dates of service. That tells us the actuaries are finally ahead of medical trend again—though 88.4% is still elevated compared to pre-2024 norms.

Dial number two is Days Claims Payable, which measures how conservatively the company reserves for unpaid hospital and doctor bills. After dipping to 44.1 days at year-end 2025, CFO Wayne DeVeydt rebuilt reserves to 48.6 days in Q1 2026 and held them steady at 47.0 days in Q2 and Q3 2026. Rising DCP paired with favorable reserve development is the gold standard of underwriting honesty.

Dials three, four, and five live inside Optum. Optum Rx is processing more than 400 million adjusted prescriptions per quarter—roughly 1.52 billion a year—with client retention in the high 90s even as it shifts toward 100% rebate pass-through. Optum Insight holds a $31 billion to $33 billion contract backlog as hospitals lean on AI automation to fight claim denials. Optum Health, however, remains the repair shop: after taking full capitation risk on 4.7 million value-based care patients and posting a $(278) million loss in FY2025, management is actively pruning loss-making contracts and exiting South America.

Dial number six is the warning light on the dashboard: CMS Medicare Advantage Star Ratings. In October 2026, CMS released the 2027 Star Ratings, and UnitedHealthcare's share of enrollees in four-star-plus plans fell from roughly 81% to between 68% and 71%, with average contract ratings slipping from 3.82 to 3.57. That doesn't hit 2026 earnings, because Star bonuses lag a year—but it creates a real revenue headwind for 2028 that management will have to offset with tighter benefit design.

Now let's do an unsparing Walk-the-Talk audit of leadership over the past five years. Between 2022 and 2024, former CEO Andrew Witty and CFO John Rex repeatedly assured Wall Street that Medicare Advantage utilization was manageable and that Optum Health's rapid capitation growth was well-controlled. Yet Change Healthcare suffered a catastrophic $2.3 billion to $2.45 billion ransomware breach due to basic perimeter gaps, V28 risk-score cuts collided with surging senior care, and 2025 guidance collapsed—forcing Witty's May 2025 exit.

Bringing back Stephen Hemsley as CEO and recruiting former Elevance Health CFO Wayne DeVeydt in September 2025 changed the tone overnight. Instead of chasing empty enrollment growth, they walked away from 1.8 million lower-margin lives in 2026, reset expectations conservatively, and then raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 in October. You and I can respect that operational discipline while keeping our eyes wide open on the unresolved DOJ billing probes and the 2027 Star Rating dip.

Look at the quarterly cadence across 2026 to see how a real turnaround builds momentum. In Q1 2026, CFO Wayne DeVeydt pushed Days Claims Payable up from 44.1 days to 48.6 days, signaling conservative reserving right out of the gate. In Q2 and Q3, DCP held firm at 47.0 days while the Medical Care Ratio fell 150 basis points year-over-year to 88.4% and Optum's operating margin expanded back to 5.5%.

That steady, sequential repair is why Stephen Hemsley's team earned the right to raise full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 in October. Yet even as the P&L heals, you and I cannot ignore the 2027 Star Rating slide to 68%–71% in four-star-plus plans. Fixing Star Ratings takes operational blocking and tackling across call centers, preventive screenings, and member satisfaction—and that will be the true test of Tim Noel and Patrick Conway over the next eighteen months.

Listen to CEO Stephen Hemsley and CFO Wayne DeVeydt on the October 13, 2026 Q3 earnings call and you hear both the confidence and the stakes. Hemsley told analysts: "Our third quarter performance reflects actions taken throughout 2026, driving meaningful progress and reinforcing our confidence to sustainably grow in 2027 and beyond within our 13% to 16% long-term target growth range." DeVeydt reinforced that message: "We are positioned to finish 2026 strongly, and we remain focused on consistently delivering our 13 to 16 percent long-term growth target." Now it is our job to hold those exact quotes against 2027 medical cost trends and 2028 Star Rating bonuses.

book_callouts.label: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.title: Why 47 Days of Reserves Matter More Than One Quarter's Beat
book_callouts.text: Any insurer can manufacture a single quarter's earnings beat by starving its claims reserves. When Days Claims Payable rises to 47.0 days alongside $610 million of favorable 2026 reserve development, it signals that the 2026 margin recovery is backed by real actuarial cushion.
